newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIAN SPIN TRIO WRECK AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN SPIN TRIO WRECK AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Indian spinners Anil Kumble, Sunil Joshi and Aashish Kapoor exploited a dry and cracked pitch to dismiss Australia for 182 on the first day of the one-off test on Thursday.
India were 57 for one at the close after losing opener Vikram Rathore for five when he was caught by Ricky Ponting at mid-wicket off paceman Paul Reiffel.
Leg-spinner Kumble snapped up four for 63, left-arm spinner Joshi captured two for 36 and Kapoor took two for 30 with his off-breaks as Australia collapsed from 81 for one.
Paceman Venkatesh Prasad and a run out accounted for the other two wickets after Australia won the toss on a surface that was expected to aid the slow bowlers.
Prasad made the initial breakthrough, trapping captain Mark Taylor lbw for 27, and Ponting was yorked by Kapoor for 14 in the last over before lunch.
Ponting's dismissal marked the start of the decline in which Australia's last nine wickets tumbled for 101.

Top scorer Michael Slater was caught and bowled by Kumble for 44, made in 130 minutes off 96 deliveries and including six fours, and Steve Waugh (0) was caught behind by a fumbling Nayan Mongia off an inside edge off Kapoor.
Mark Waugh and Michael Bevan briefly checked the slide by adding 49 for the fifth wicket before Bevan, playing across the line, was trapped leg before by Joshi for 26.
Waugh also made 26 before falling to Joshi, and Kumble then polished off the lower order, the last six wickets crashing for 39.
India started painfully slowly with Mongia struggling for 40 minutes in a shaky role as opener before hitting the first four of the innings. He was unbeaten on 26 at the close.

But left-hander Saurav Ganguly, playing his third test after a century each in his first two tests in England this year, struck four fours in his unbeaten 19, two off the medium pace of Steve Waugh in one over and two more from a single over by debutant left-arm spinner Brad Hogg.
India brought in medium-fast bowler David Johnson in place of fellow Bangalore paceman Javagal Srinath, who was declared unfit with a stiff shoulder.
Johnson, 23, is of Anglo-Indian parentage, and toured Sri Lanka and Canada with the Indian team for one-day games this year.
Australian coach Geoff Marsh said: "We did play a couple of loose strokes but the Indian spinners bowled extremely well.
"We'd have liked to score 50 or 60 more runs but the game is still wide open. The ball's turning and its keeping up and down.
"We are very much in the game," he said, adding that his spinners had not bowled much until now and the Indian batsmen's real test would be on Friday morning.
"Our spinners have just bowled three overs each and they can be menacing with the old ball," he said.
